correctness.rationale: Itô raw second moments are valid for any finite-second-moment initial law; their exact linear combination cancels all other raw moments. This gives the nonautonomous scalar response and stationary preparation. A strictly positive convolution kernel yields an unattainable-earlier-zero lower bound, and a positive-temperature constant extremal protocol attains the bound uniquely up to common heating. Critical parameters are a,b>0,ab>c^2,c!=0, positive locally bounded measurable baths, Delta(t)>=-B, Delta0,B>0. 2100 independent numerical diagnostic comparisons passed; finite tests are not used as a proof.

value.rationale: The precisely specified angular-current moment is experimentally interpretable as torque/circulation, but ordinarily tied to three covariance moments. Showing a universal single relaxation mode under arbitrary bath driving and a sharp achievable first reversal constraint yields a natural design and diagnostic rule that differs from stationarity and full-state equilibration optimization. It is not merely a numerical tweak.
